name: Connecticut
rateNote: Annual rate on full purchase price — 6-month standard redemption window
auctionPlatform: Township-run — 169 townships across 8 counties each run independent sales
keyNotes: 169 townships each run independent sales — no centralized system
Deed executed within 2 weeks, held unrecorded at town clerk for 6-month window
After redemption expires: deed records, title passes free and clear
18% annualized but effective return is ~9% if redeemed at 6-month mark
Abandoned property: redemption window shrinks to 60 days
summary: Connecticut municipalities independently elect to sell tax liens or redeemable deeds. No centralized state platform. 1-year redemption. Statute: CGS §12-157.
typeWhy: Connecticut municipalities sell tax lien certificates, giving investors the right to collect delinquent taxes with interest. The property owner retains title during the 1-year redemption period. CGS §12-157.
rateWhy: Connecticut imposes an 18% statutory penalty on redemption — this is a flat penalty structure rather than a compounding annual interest rate. CGS §12-157.
notBeginnerReason: Each municipality independently chooses between lien and redeemable deed format. Requires individual research per town.
beginnerTip: Contact tax collectors in Waterbury, Bridgeport, and Hartford — these cities have higher delinquency rates and more consistent sale schedules than smaller towns.
risks: Format (lien vs. redeemable deed) varies by town — confirm before registering
No centralized state system — requires individual municipality research
Higher-value towns (Greenwich, Westport) rarely have delinquencies worth pursuing
ddExtra: Confirm the sale format with the town tax collector before any due diligence
Verify lien priority — Connecticut has complex municipal lien priority rules
Check for any active municipal code violations on occupied structures

steps: Identify your target municipality at portal.ct.gov
Contact the Town Tax Collector directly — ask if they conduct lien or redeemable deed sales and when the next sale is scheduled
Register per the town's specific instructions — most require in-person registration

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

stateStructure.CRITICAL: Connecticut has NO county government for tax purposes. 169 towns/cities each operate independently. No statewide auction portal.
stateStructure.salesNotices: Public notices posted at cttaxsales.com (unofficial aggregator) and in local newspapers
stateStructure.enforcement: Municipality (town/city) tax collector initiates — may also use: judicial foreclosure (CGS §12-181) or lien assignment

auction.frequency: As scheduled by municipality — no statewide uniform date
auction.platform: In-person at town hall or online (varies by municipality and attorney handling sale)
auction.minimumBid: Generally covers delinquent taxes + interest + charges
auction.auctioneerFee: Town may hire auctioneer — cost added to delinquent taxpayer's debt (CGS §12-157(d))
auction.deed: Collector's Deed executed within 2 weeks of sale. Lodged unrecorded at Town Clerk for 6-month redemption period.

otc.name: Lien Assignment
otc.description: Municipalities may assign (sell) tax liens to private parties individually or in bulk
otc.note: Broad leeway to negotiate amount paid; requires approval of town's legislative body. Contact town tax collector directly.

subTax.name: N/A — CT tax sale structure does not have lien cert sub-tax mechanism

redemption.abandonedPeriod: 60 days (if abandoned or meets conditions established by town ordinance)
redemption.rate: 18% per annum on TOTAL purchase price paid by buyer
redemption.otherInterest: Owner must also pay outstanding taxes + charges + any amounts owed municipality not recovered by sale
redemption.federalLien: Federal government redeems at 0.5%/month (lower rate) — may have separate redemption window
redemption.afterRedemption: If redeemed — deed returned to taxpayer. Escrow funds returned to purchaser within 10 days.
redemption.note: Title passes FREE AND CLEAR once 6-month period expires WITHOUT redemption. All prior liens extinguished — limited exceptions.

deedPath.name: Collector's Deed (Tax Sale Deed)
deedPath.titleQuality: Free and clear of prior liens after redemption period — with exceptions: non-monetary encumbrances (easements, covenants), municipal charges not recovered, IRS redemption right
deedPath.titleInsuranceNote: Most title companies won't insure until 1+ year after Collector's Deed is recorded

surplus.name: Excess Proceeds / Overbid
surplus.trigger: Sale price exceeds all delinquent taxes + interest + penalties + costs
surplus.ifRedeemed: Escrow returned to purchaser within 10 days of redemption
surplus.ifNotRedeemed: Escrow may be used to pay other taxes on taxpayer's property; any remaining paid to Superior Court clerk for distribution to rightful parties
surplus.note: Tyler v. Hennepin — CT's process routes surplus to court for distribution, consistent with constitutional requirement

rules.lienValidity: 15 years — taxes not collected after 15 years deemed uncollectible (with exceptions)

es.summary: Los municipios de Connecticut eligen independientemente vender gravámenes o escrituras redimibles. Sin plataforma estatal centralizada. Redención de 1 año. Estatuto: CGS §12-157.
es.typeWhy: Connecticut es un estado de gravamen donde cada municipio vende gravámenes fiscales con un período de redención de 1 año (CGS §12-157).
es.rateWhy: La penalización fija del 18% proporciona un retorno sólido y predecible. Esta tasa no se puja a la baja (CGS §12-157).
es.notBeginnerReason: Cada municipio elige independientemente entre gravamen y escritura redimible. Requiere investigación individual por ciudad.
es.beginnerTip: Contacte recaudadores en Waterbury, Bridgeport y Hartford — estas ciudades tienen mayor morosidad y calendarios más consistentes.
risks: El formato varía por ciudad — confirme antes de registrarse
Las ciudades de alto valor (Greenwich, Westport) rara vez tienen morosidades que valgan la pena
ddExtra: Confirme el formato de venta con el recaudador antes de cualquier diligencia debida
Verifique la prioridad del gravamen — CT tiene reglas complejas de prioridad municipal
Revise violaciones activas del código municipal en estructuras ocupadas

auctionSignup.platform: Específico por ciudad — contacte cada municipio directamente
steps: Identifique su municipio objetivo en portal.ct.gov
Contacte al Recaudador de Impuestos directamente — pregunte el formato y cuándo es la próxima venta
Solicite la lista de propiedades en mora
Regístrese según instrucciones de la ciudad — la mayoría requiere registro en persona
